claims.quote: Vashti isolated herself—it was necessary, for neither day nor night existed under the ground—and reviewed all that had happened since she had summoned the bed last.
claims.description: Most of humanity lives in individual rooms deep underground, with artificial light and no day or night.

claims.quote: presently she could see the image of her son, who lived on the other side of the earth, and he could see her.
claims.description: A handheld plate carries live two-way video calls across the globe.

claims.quote: There were buttons and switches everywhere—buttons to call for food, for music, for clothing.
claims.description: A fully automated room supplies food, music, clothing and more at the press of a button.

claims.quote: There was the hot-bath button, by pressure of which a basin of (imitation) marble rose out of the floor, filled to the brim with a warm deodorised liquid.
claims.description: Automated room fixtures such as a bath rise from the floor on demand.

claims.quote: There was the button that produced literature.
claims.description: A button delivers any literature on demand.

claims.quote: The clumsy system of public gatherings had been long since abandoned; neither Vashti nor her audience stirred from their rooms.
claims.description: Lectures and meetings are held remotely, each person in their own room, hearing and seeing the speaker by machine.

claims.quote: The air-ship barely takes two days to fly between me and you.
claims.description: Air-ships carry passengers between hemispheres in about two days.

claims.quote: In it were instructions against every possible contingency.
claims.description: A guidebook for the Machine contains instructions for every situation, and people ritually revere it.

claims.quote: She would summon a car and it would fly with her down the tunnel until it reached the lift that communicated with the air-ship station
claims.description: Automated cars travel through tunnels and lifts to air-ship stations.

claims.quote: Immediately an enormous apparatus fell on to her out of the ceiling, a thermometer was automatically inserted between her lips, a stethoscope was automatically laid upon her heart.
claims.description: Automated medical apparatus examines a patient and a remote doctor treats her.

claims.quote: Few travelled in these days, for, thanks to the advance of science, the earth was exactly alike all over.
claims.description: Technology makes every place on Earth uniform, so people stop traveling.

claims.quote: The forests had been destroyed during the literature epoch for the purpose of making newspaper-pulp
claims.description: Forests are cleared for newspaper pulp.

claims.quote: Homelessness means death. The victim is exposed to the air, which kills him.
claims.description: Offenders against the Machine are punished by exposure to the lethal outer air.

claims.quote: Each infant was examined at birth, and all who promised undue strength were destroyed.
claims.description: Strong infants are killed at birth because strength is considered undesirable.

claims.quote: The surface of the earth is only dust and mud, no life remains on it, and you would need a respirator, or the cold of the outer air would kill you.
claims.description: The Earth's surface becomes uninhabitable to unprotected humans.

claims.quote: one simply summons a respirator and gets an Egression-permit
claims.description: Going outside requires a respirator and an official egression permit.

claims.quote: All the fear and the superstition that existed once have been destroyed by the Machine.
claims.description: Religion disappears, replaced by an unacknowledged worship of the Machine.

claims.quote: all the food-tubes and medicine-tubes and music-tubes that the Machine has evolved lately
claims.description: Tube networks deliver food, medicine and music throughout the underground cities.

claims.quote: For Kuno had lately asked to be a father, and his request had been refused by the Committee.
claims.description: A central Committee controls who is allowed to have children.
